item.title: Democratic Socialists of America propose radical overhaul of US govt - The Democratic Socialists of America want to fight for working-class Americans by offering free healthcare and abolishing the U.S. Senate.
item.description: The recently released platform for the Democratic Socialists of America is titled "Workers Deserve More" and it includes some proposals to ease cost of living for working families that are popular among many progressives, such as free healthcare and pre-K. "You have no debt. You don’t need health insurance," the platform’s website says, laying out its vision for American social democracy. "You don’t pay a mortgage or have a landlord, because comfortable housing is a human right." The platform, released July 14, drew widespread backlash from conservatives. Republican Speaker of the House Mike Johnson reacted to the platform calling it "communism" by "barbarians," while slamming the more radical policies like eliminating the U.S. Senate or having the president selected by Congress. "This isn’t just Common Sense vs. Crazy anymore," Johnson wrote on X. "It’s Common Sense vs. COMMUNISM." Although not all self-described democratic socialists are in the Democratic Socialists of America, the DSA is an increasingly influential player on the left. Members include New York Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Michigan Rep. Rashida Tlaib, all Democrats. Three Democratic nominees for U.S. House of Representative seats – Darializa Avila Chevalier and Claire Valdez in New York and Melat Kiros in Colorado – also belong to the group, as do a growing list of state and local officials. A third of Democrats identify as democratic socialists, according to a July 30 CNN poll, but it's possible that quite a few of those are not familiar with some of the DSA's more unusual suggestions for overhauling the U.S. government. A July 28 Reuters/Ipsos poll revealed that 47% of Americans say they don't understand democratic socialist policies. While President Donald Trump and his GOP allies slam democratic socialists as "communists," the Democratic Socialists of America is defining its own brand in the new platform. The 120,000-member organization's policy roadmap has three sections: Thriving Working-Class Communities Working-Class Foreign Policy Working-Class Democracy Reforming democracy "Working-Class Democracy" aims to increase access to the electoral system by expanding voting rights beyond citizens to all permanent residents. It would also restore the right to vote to those stripped of it for a criminal conviction, and it calls for statehood for Washington, DC, and self-determination of U.S. territories, such as Puerto Rico and Guam. The platform also calls for structural changes, some of which would require amending the U.S. Constitution, including: Abolishing the U.S. Senate. Democratic Socialists of America co-chair Megan Romer told FOX News that the Senate is an "anachronistic institution. It comes from the British House of Lords," and was created to "protect power" and ensure "the people didn't have too much of a say. Expanding the House of Representatives to an unspecified number Replacing the two-party system with a "multi-party democracy" Abolishing the Electoral College and having Congress elect the president and Supreme Court Implementing ranked-choice voting in all elections Ridding the system of lobbyists and “dark money” - or funding from election Super PACs who do not need to disclose donors On businesses, the platform calls for making large corporations public, implementing "aggressive wealth taxes" and empowering workers to unionize. https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2026/08/02/democratic-socialists-america-platform/91092595007/

item.title: The timeline of Jimothy.
item.description:
2026 is a weird year.
Jimmothy is amazing though, and probably one of the best things we got this year. Front page edit: Sorry I've not really been around for those that like to conversate. I hit a new type of burnout that physically affected me pretty seriously. I'm fine, don't sweat it. Just would like to explain the absence of my commentary for the few that care. - I'm depressed. Many of us are. But knowing that I was part of the military intelligence sphere here in America, not only but a few decades ago, not even, was I helping write the book and practice the new standard procedures for not collecting on United States citizens. This came after Bush and was implemented pretty seriously. We vet our targets. We verify the need to collect, and we don't overstep any jurisdictions we don't need to. And we correct any issues that we see that do try to broach any illegal activity. I was proud. I felt like we were making change. And now, look at this. Flock cameras everywhere. And other making a change. And now, look at this. Flot cameras everywhere. And other implementations I can't even begin to describe. I never thought America would fall for this bullshit or allow it. And, in light of things, it seems like people are wising up to this bullshit. Don't look for heroes. This isn't a Hollywood movie. This is history in the making.

item.title: GovBrief Today #549
item.description: Illinois went and found the people Washington stopped feeding. About 148,000 Illinois residents have lost food assistance since new federal work rules hit in May, veterans, people in their sixties, and parents of teenagers among them. On Saturday the state began depositing $400 onto the grocery cards of every affected person. Nobody had to fill out a form. The state did all the work. Washington changed the rules betting families would trip over the paperwork, and 148,000 of them did. Illinois ran the same lists in the opposite direction. It's one payment, about two months of groceries, and Governor Pritzker says no state can backfill what Congress cut. But this weekend, Illinois treated caring for its hungry as its job.
